original_question: Is there a mitochondrial enzyme regulated by N-acetylglutamate whose deficiency can lead to the accumulation of ammonia in the blood?

final_qi.question: Is there a mitochondrial enzyme regulated by N-acetylglutamate whose deficiency can lead to the accumulation of ammonia in the blood?
final_qi.long_answer: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS-I) is the first, mitochondrial enzyme of the urea cycle. It requires the allosteric activator N-acetylglutamate for full activity. Genetic deficiency of CPS-I impairs conversion of ammonia to carbamoyl phosphate, leading to accumulation of ammonia in the blood (hyperammonemia).

0.question: Which mitochondrial enzyme is regulated by N-acetylglutamate?

final_answer.long_answer: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS I) is the first mitochondrial enzyme of the urea cycle. It is allosterically activated by N-acetylglutamate. When CPS I is deficient, ammonia cannot be converted into carbamoyl phosphate, preventing entry into the urea cycle and resulting in marked accumulation of ammonia in the bloodstream (hyperammonemia).
